About Us

Black Elk Espresso is a busy and well-established café located in Carnes Hill, known for its quality food, premium coffee and exceptional customer service. We pride ourselves on providing a welcoming atmosphere, efficient service and a consistently high standard of hospitality for our customers.

Our café serves a diverse clientele, including local residents, families and professionals, and operates in a fast-paced environment throughout weekdays and weekends. We are committed to maintaining excellent operational standards while fostering a positive and supportive workplace for our team.

Role

Black Elk Espresso is seeking an experienced and motivated Venue Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of the venue. The position involves managing daily business operations, supervising staff, monitoring financial performance, maintaining exceptional customer service standards, and ensuring the efficient and profitable operation of the café.

The Venue Manager will oversee staffing, budgeting, stock control, supplier relationships and venue operations while ensuring compliance with food safety, workplace health and safety, and licensing requirements. Applicants must possess strong leadership, organisational and communication skills, together with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced hospitality environment.

Responsibilities and Duties

Oversee the day-to-day operations of the venue to ensure efficient service and a high standard of customer satisfaction.
Manage, recruit, train, supervise and mentor front and back-of-house staff, ensuring appropriate staffing levels and performance standards.
Prepare and manage staff rosters, monitor labour costs and allocate duties to maximise operational efficiency.
Monitor venue performance, sales, operating costs and budgets, and implement strategies to improve profitability and business performance.
Manage stock ordering, inventory levels and supplier relationships to ensure the timely supply of goods and minimise wastage.
Ensure exceptional customer service by responding to customer enquiries, resolving complaints and maintaining positive customer relationships.
Develop, implement and monitor operational policies and procedures to maintain consistent service standards.
Ensure compliance with food safety legislation, workplace health and safety requirements, licensing obligations and company policies.
Monitor the presentation, cleanliness and maintenance of the venue to ensure a safe and welcoming environment for customers and staff.
Liaise with senior management regarding business performance, staffing requirements, promotional activities and operational improvements.
Analyse financial and operational reports and implement initiatives to improve efficiency, productivity and customer experience.
Coordinate special events, promotions and marketing initiatives to increase customer engagement and venue performance.

Skills and Qualifications

AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma (OSCA Skill Level 2).
At least 3 years of relevant work experience.
Demonstrated experience managing a café, restaurant or hospitality venue.
Strong leadership, organisational and communication skills.
Ability to manage staff, coordinate daily operations and maintain high customer service standards in a fast-paced hospitality environment.
Sound understanding of budgeting, stock control, food safety, workplace health and safety, and hospitality compliance requirements.
Hardworking, positive attitude, and ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
Flexibility to work weekdays, weekends and public holidays as required.

Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.

Salary: $79,500

•	Install, maintain, and repair plumbing systems, fixtures, pipes, and associated equipment in line with the Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA) and AS/NZS 3500.

•	Complete comprehensive plumbing work for residential and commercial new builds, renovations, fit-outs, and system upgrades.

•	Diagnose complex faults, clear blockages, isolate leaks, and carry out corrective repairs.

•	Read and interpret plans, architectural blueprints, technical specifications, and compliance documentation.

•	Liaise with clients, contractors, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth project delivery.

•	Ensure all work complies with NSW plumbing, drainage, and gas fitting safety regulations.

•	Maintain accurate job records, reports, and compliance documentation, including contributing to Certificates of Compliance (CoC).

•	Contribute to continuous improvement and uphold high industry service standards.

To be successfully considered for this role you will:

 *  Be qualified to Certificate IV level or agreed equivalent 

 *  Hold,  or be eligible to acquire, all relevant certificates enabling employment in NSW.

 *  Have at least one or more  years of relevant plumbing experience in residential or commercial settings (incorporating new installations, maintenance, and repairs).

 *  Possess strong technical skills across water supply, sanitary plumbing, drainage, and general plumbing systems.

 *  Hold, or be eligible to acquire, a  General Construction Induction Card (White Card).

*   Possess a valid Australian Driver’s Licence.

 *  Demonstrate strong communication, customer service, and independent task-management skills.

 *  Provide solid professional references upon request.

•	Verification of Competency (VOC) or Statement of Attainment (SOA) excavator ticket.

•	Confined Spaces Rescuer certification (Sydney Water Procedure - WHSMS0068).

•	Work Safely at Heights certification.

•	First Aid certification.

Central Adelaide Local Health Network (CALHN)

Port Augusta 

Salary MDP-2 $99,707 - $158,523 p.a.+ super + salary packaging

Full-time temporary 

Duration of the training program: 12 months from 1-2-27 up to 30-1-28

Term of the Contract: 3 Years in line with clause 52 of the Salaried Medical Officers Enterprise Agreement

At the end of the training program, CALHN will work with the employee to find a suitable placement within SA Health for the remainder of the 3 year contract.

Grow Your Medical Career With Us
Join CALHN's exceptional medical team and play a vital role in shaping the future of health through innovation, collaboration and world-class care.

Work across diverse clinical specialties and services

Advance your skills through structured learning and development

Benefit from supportive teams and dedicated non-clinical time

Make a real impact delivering safe and connected compassionate care

Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN

About the Role

oin our team as a Service Registrar and play a key role in delivering high quality patient care across the service. You will assess, manage and coordinate care for surgical patients, work closely with Consultants and multidisciplinary teams, and help shape a supportive learning environment through teaching, mentoring and continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities

- Manage the care of patients under Consultant supervision
- Assess new referrals from the Emergency Department, wards and specialist teams
- Coordinate timely reviews, admissions, transfers and discharges
- Support the care of emergency surgical patients across the wards
- Assist in theatre as required
- Work closely with Consultants and multidisciplinary teams
- Liaise with Pathology, Radiology, Emergency, Outpatients and Theatre services
- Communicate clearly with patients and families to support informed care
- Build strong relationships with GPs and community referrers
- Mentor, supervise and support junior medical staff
- Contribute to quality improvement and ongoing education
- Respond professionally to patient and family feedback

About You

You are a collaborative and patient focused medical professional who thrives in a busy clinical environment. You bring sound clinical judgement, excellent communication skills and a commitment to delivering safe, high quality care.

- MBBS or equivalent medical qualification
- General registration with the Medical Board of Australia
- Build strong relationships across multidisciplinary teams
- Make sound clinical decisions and solve complex problems
- Commit to quality improvement and patient centred care

Why You'll Love It Here - CALHN benefits that matter
We know that a great career is about more than just the work you do, it's also about the support you receive. At CALHN, you'll enjoy :

Salary packaging - up to $9,010 for living expenses + $2,650 for meals & entertainment + pre-tax super & novated lease options

Safe connections - be part of a culture of safety and connectivity, focusing on outcomes and continuous improvements

Professional development - funding + study leave for growth opportunities

Recognition & growth - celebrate success and explore opportunities across CALHN's many sites

Flexible work options - speak to us about flexibility options for this role to suit your lifestyle

 Paid leave - with leave loading for rest and recharge

Health & fitness perks - discounted access to Fitness Passport & free flu vaccinations

Wellbeing support - Employee Assistance Program for you & your family

Diversity & Inclusion
We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, culturally diverse backgrounds, and LGBTQIA+ communities.
